clips.text: Almost every stranger who talks to you will ask some version of the same four or five questions. That's good news — it means you can walk in with real answers ready, instead of building each one from scratch under pressure.
¿De dónde eres?
Answer with where you're actually from. Speak now.
Soy de Estados Unidos.
¿Cuánto tiempo te vas a quedar?
This one wants a real number, not a philosophy. Keep it short.
Give your real length of stay. Speak now.
Diez días, más o menos.
¿Qué te ha gustado más de México?
This is the question that makes the conversation warm instead of transactional. A specific answer lands better than a generic 'everything' — it shows you were actually paying attention.
Give one specific thing you've genuinely liked. Speak now.
Me encantó la comida, sobre todo los tacos.
¿Vienes solo o con familia?
Say who you're travelling with, or that you're on your own. Speak now.
Vengo con mi pareja.
And if you want out of a conversation, that's fine too — one polite line closes it without rudeness.
You need to get going. Excuse yourself politely. Speak now.
Bueno, fue un gusto. Que le vaya bien.
Soy de Estados Unidos. Diez días, más o menos. Me encantó la comida.

I05 complete. Origin, duration, what you've liked, who you're with — the same four questions, almost every time. Have your real answers ready, and the fifth skill, leaving a conversation politely, is just as useful as staying in one.
A friendly stranger asks the same handful of questions travellers hear constantly. Listen for the ready answers and the polite exit.
¿De dónde eres?
Soy de Estados Unidos.
¿Qué te ha gustado más de México?
Me encantó la comida, sobre todo los tacos.
